years_since_diagnosis.evidence: dealing with Crohn's for about ten years now

occupation.evidence: Work in IT, thankfully can work from home when needed

location.evidence: Initially misdiagnosed with UC (colonic involvement implied), then small bowel follow-through showed involvement beyond the colon; strictures requiring resection of ~30cm small intestine — both small bowel and colon involved

severity.evidence: Required surgical resection, failed multiple biologics, has strictures, short bowel syndrome, crushing fatigue, ongoing symptoms disrupting sleep

disease_control.evidence: On Stelara for two years but Crohn's symptoms often wake him at night; GI pushing for combo therapy suggesting incomplete control; fatigue described as 'crushing some days'

treatments.evidence: Post-surgery, started on methotrexate, helped for a while but developed lung problems, possibly drug-related
Switched to Humira, miraculous for three years, then stopped working
Insurance wouldn't cover Stelara without failing another anti-TNF first, so tried Remicade. Developed antibodies within six months.
Finally got Stelara approved, been on it for two years. The every 8-week injection is manageable, though expensive even with insurance.

encounters.evidence: Initially misdiagnosed with ulcerative colitis — implies initial presentation to a provider before specialist referral
Took two years to get the correct Crohn's diagnosis after a small bowel follow-through showed involvement beyond the colon
By then, I'd already developed strictures requiring surgical resection. Lost about 30cm of small intestine.

Post-surgery, started on methotrexate... Switched to Humira... tried Remicade... Finally got Stelara approved. Dr. Anderson, my GI, is pushing for combo therapy - adding methotrexate back at lower dose with Stelara.

status.evidence: Finally got Stelara approved, been on it for two years.

barriers.evidence: Insurance wouldn't cover Stelara without failing another anti-TNF first, so tried Remicade.
expensive even with insurance. Copay assistance program helps, but always worried it'll end.

referral_steps_gp_to_prescriber.evidence: GP/initial provider -> GI specialist (diagnosis and treatment) = 2 steps to biologic prescriber

extraction_notes: Patient was initially misdiagnosed with UC; correct Crohn's diagnosis came after small bowel follow-through. Surgical resection preceded biologic use. Step therapy required Remicade trial before Stelara insurance approval. B12 injections, vitamin D, iron infusions excluded from treatments as nutritional supplements for short bowel syndrome comorbidity. CPAP excluded as unrelated to Crohn's. Antidepressants excluded as unrelated comorbidity treatment. Combo therapy (adding low-dose methotrexate to Stelara) is currently being discussed/pushed by GI but patient is hesitant due to prior lung issues — not yet started, so not added to treatment list. Disease control set to 'partial' as Stelara provides some benefit but symptoms persist (night waking, fatigue).
